title: Linear Search and Algorithm Tracing
intro: A short, self-paced catch-up covering the essential lesson ideas. Check every question, then correct anything missed.

stages.label: Remember
stages.lead: Retrieve two ideas from earlier learning.

questions.prompt: What does a linear search require from the list?
questions.feedback: Linear search can scan unsorted data.

questions.prompt: What does the CPU fetch stage do?
questions.feedback: Fetch retrieves the instruction to decode.

stages.label: Learn
stages.lead: Read the key concepts, visual model and worked explanation.

blocks.title: A sequential scan
blocks.text: Linear search starts at one end of a collection and compares one element at a time with the target.

blocks.title: Zero-based indices
blocks.text: The first array element is at index 0, then 1, 2, etc. Do not confuse index with value.

blocks.title: Stopping
blocks.text: If the target is found, report its index. If the list ends without a match, report not found.

blocks.title: One strength
blocks.text: Linear search works even if values are unsorted, though it may need to inspect the entire list.

blocks.title: Visual model · Linear Search and Algorithm Tracing
blocks.caption: Linear search checks successive items and can report the first matching zero-based index.

blocks.title: Worked example · Trace linear search for 8 in [3, 9, 1, 8, 5]. Give the comparisons and index.
blocks.text: Start at index 0 and compare 3 with 8: no match. Index 1: 9 is not 8. Index 2: 1 is not 8. Index 3: 8 matches the target. Report found at index 3 after four comparisons.

items: linear search — Checks items one by one for a target.
index — Position used to access an array item, starting at zero.
comparison — Checking an item against a value or condition.

questions.prompt: Where does a zero-based array begin?
questions.feedback: The first item is at index 0.

questions.prompt: When does a successful linear search stop?
options: Only after checking every item twice
questions.feedback: It can stop when an item equals the target.

questions.prompt: Can linear search find an item in an unsorted list?
options: Only if the target is the last item
questions.feedback: It checks items in sequence, so sorting is unnecessary.

stages.label: Practise
stages.lead: Match and reorder before applying the method yourself.

blocks.text: Distinguish the item value from its position; count indexes from zero.

questions.prompt: Match the zero-based index to the item in [7,2,6].
questions.feedback: Indices count positions from zero, not values.

stages.label: Apply
stages.lead: Predict the Code First result and write one exam-style answer.

blocks.title: Code First · Predict → Write → Test → Improve
blocks.caption: Predict the index printed. Change the target to "MDR". State what the PC and MDR hold in a real CPU.

blocks.text: Explain how linear search would find 7 in an unsorted list [3, 8, 7, 1], or report failure. [4 marks]

questions.prompt: In [MAR, MDR, PC], which zero-based index contains PC?
questions.feedback: MAR is index 0, MDR index 1, PC index 2.

questions.prompt: Change the search target to MDR. What zero-based index is returned?
questions.feedback: MDR is the second element, at index 1.

questions.prompt: Search [9, 4, 1, 6] for 1. At which zero-based index is it found?

writing.prompt: Explain how linear search would find 7 in an unsorted list [3, 8, 7, 1], or report failure. [4 marks]
writing.model: Start at first element [1]; compare sequentially 3, 8, 7 [1]; report index 2 when found [1]; if end reached with no match report not found [1].
checklist: I described how comparison starts at the first item.
I explained how the search proceeds and where it stops.
I stated the found index or not-found result.

stages.label: Check
stages.lead: Check your understanding and review your mastery result.

questions.prompt: Linear search can work on unsorted items.
questions.feedback: It checks values one by one without relying on sort order.

questions.prompt: The first item in a zero-based array is at index 1.
questions.feedback: The first array item is index 0.

questions.prompt: Linear search must report not found if the list ends without a match.
questions.feedback: An unsuccessful search exhausts the available items.
